components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-site-header { display: flex; min-height: 104px; align-items: flex-end; justify-content: space-between; gap: 40px; padding: 30px 0 20px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--strong-rule, #7a828e); color: var(--ink, #1b1d20); } .ds-site-mark { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 11px; } .ds-site-mark span { color: var(--muted, #626974); font: 11px/1.6 "SUIT", system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; letter-spacing: .08em; } .ds-site-title { color: var(--ink, #1b1d20); font: 700 34px/1 "Maru Buri", serif; letter-spacing: -.025em; text-decoration: none; } .ds-site-title:hover { color: var(--link, #1646d8); } .ds-site-nav { display: flex; gap: 22px; font: 600 13px/1.6 "SUIT", system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-site-nav a { color: var(--link, #1646d8); text-decoration: none; } .ds-site-nav a:hover { color: var(--signal, #d83a28); } .ds-site-nav .ds-current { color: var(--ink, #1b1d20); text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--signal, #d83a28); text-decoration-thickness: 2px; text-underline-offset: 7px; } .ds-site-nav a:focus-visible, .ds-site-title:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal, #d83a28); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Topic Register

components.css: .ds-topic-register { display: grid; width: 184px; color: var(--ink, #1b1d20); font: 13px/1.6 "SUIT", system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-topic-register strong { padding-bottom: 9px; border-bottom: 2px solid var(--ink, #1b1d20); font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: .08em; } .ds-topic-register button { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr auto; min-height: 40px; align-items: center; gap: 16px; border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #c6cbd2); border-radius: 0; padding: 5px 0; background: transparent; color: var(--link, #1646d8); font: inherit; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; } .ds-topic-register button:hover { color: var(--signal, #d83a28); } .ds-topic-register .ds-current { color: var(--ink, #1b1d20); font-weight: 750; } .ds-topic-register .ds-current span::before { color: var(--signal, #d83a28); content: "— "; } .ds-topic-register small { color: var(--muted, #626974); font-size: 11px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-topic-register button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal, #d83a28); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.css: .ds-record-list { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; color: var(--ink, #1b1d20); } .ds-record { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 42px minmax(0, 1fr) 190px; gap: 0 16px; min-height: 72px; align-items: center; padding: 12px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #c6cbd2); } .ds-sequence { color: var(--muted, #626974); font: 11px/1.6 "SUIT", system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-record-title { position: relative; justify-self: start; border: 0; padding: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--ink, #1b1d20); font: 700 18px/1.45 "Maru Buri", serif; letter-spacing: -.015em; cursor: pointer; } .ds-record-title::after { position: absolute; right: 0; bottom: -3px; left: 0; height: 2px; transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left; background: var(--link, #1646d8); content: ""; transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1); } .ds-record-title:hover { color: var(--link, #1646d8); } .ds-record-title:hover::after { transform: scaleX(1); } .ds-record-title:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal, #d83a28); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-record-title:active { color: var(--signal, #d83a28); } .ds-record-meta { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: 10px; color: var(--muted, #626974); font: 11px/1.6 "SUIT", system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-record-meta time { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-topic { color: var(--link, #1646d8); font-weight: 650; } .ds-new { color: var(--signal, #d83a28); font-weight: 750; white-space: nowrap; }

narrative.overview:
Wlog is a personal publication shaped as a working index rather than a stream, dashboard, or replica of another plain-text blog. Cool-gray paper, aligned record rows, and terse annotations give it the authority of an actively maintained register. The publication begins with writing and trusts sequence, title, topic, and date to explain the collection.

The visual system deliberately splits voices. Self-hosted Maru Buri gives the masthead, titles, and prose a literary editorial character; self-hosted SUIT keeps navigation, counts, dates, controls, and administrator forms exact and operational. Cobalt always helps the reader move, while vermilion marks current state, freshness, focus, errors, and decisive hover feedback.
keyCharacteristics: A cool-gray, 1120px page frame with a 760px record index and 150–184px topic register.
A 34px Maru Buri masthead, thin gray header rule, and writing immediately in the first viewport.
Numbered rows aligning serif titles against SUIT dates, topics, and freshness states.
Cobalt navigation and action color, with vermilion reserved for state and response.
Square, ruled fields and fieldsets that keep owner configuration inside the publication world.
A semantic dark inversion and responsive single-axis reading path.

rules.name: The Cobalt-Leads Rule
rules.body: Cobalt denotes routes, filters, focus, and primary action; it is functional indexing ink, never ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Vermilion-Responds Rule
rules.body: Vermilion appears only when something is current, fresh, progressing, invalid, focused, or actively responding.

rules.name: The Semantic Inversion Rule
rules.body: Dark appearance changes token values, not hierarchy, geometry, density, or component roles.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Maru Buri owns authored content and editorial hierarchy; SUIT owns navigation, metadata, controls, and system feedback.

rules.name: The Tabular Record Rule
rules.body: Dates, years, counts, and row numbers use tabular numerals so the index reads by columns rather than by decoration.

rules.name: The Immediate-Index Rule
rules.body: The first viewport contains the masthead, thin rule, recent-post heading and count, numbered records, and—when width permits—the topic register. No hero or introductory panel precedes them.

rules.name: The Aligned-Record Rule
rules.body: Preserve the relationship between sequence, title, date, topic, and state. When space tightens, stack metadata beneath the title rather than discarding the sequence or turning records into cards.

rules.name: The Flat-Register Rule
rules.body: Persistent information stays in the document plane; rules and tonal paper changes carry structure, and shadow is reserved for transient feedback.

rules.name: The Square-Annotation Rule
rules.body: Operational elements may be bordered, filled, or underlined, but their corners remain square so they read as annotations on a working document.

rules.name: The Shared-Publication Rule
rules.body: Reading and administrator forms use the same paper, rules, type roles, and semantic colors; administration never splits into a dashboard world.

dos: Do begin with the 34px masthead, thin header rule, recent-post heading and count, and numbered writing records.
Do keep desktop records aligned as sequence, title, date, topic, and state within the 760px index.
Do use Maru Buri for editorial hierarchy and prose, and SUIT for interface language and metadata.
Do use cobalt for navigation and action, and vermilion for current, fresh, progress, focus, error, and active response.
Do preserve square controls, visible keyboard focus, dark-token inversion, safe areas, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do keep owner configuration honest and visibly part of the same publication grammar.
donts: Don't copy the composition of the atmospheric reference or regress to a generic plain-text blog list.
Don't introduce a hero, manifesto, promotional introduction, or marketing call to action before the writing.
Don't turn records, topics, articles, or settings into rounded cards, pills, dashboard tiles, or thumbnail feeds.
Don't collapse the two-voice type system into all-serif or all-interface typography.
Don't use cobalt or vermilion as general decoration, or replace aligned metadata with loose badges.
Don't imply RSS behavior, production authentication, secure password persistence, or backend publishing through visual affordances.
